status.en: 4 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 79% fewer than the week before, most of them in La Espriella, Espriella and Planadas.
status.nb: 4 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 79 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i La Espriella, Espriella og Planadas.

summary.en: President De la Espriella is confronting a wave of armed violence after a police academy attack killed 21 people and nationwide protests erupted over tax plans and spending cuts. He ordered a tenth bombing against a narcoterrorist target in Valle del Cauca and urged the United States to prosecute former President Petro. U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth arrived in Bogotá, delivered a C-130, met De la Espriella and announced a US-Venezuela military partnership, while Colombia rejected a U.S. proposal for joint anti-drug strikes. The conflict recorded 225 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
